records.source: לַמְנַצֵּ֣חַ אַל־תַּשְׁחֵת֮ לְדָוִ֪ד מִ֫כְתָּ֥ם בִּשְׁלֹ֥חַ שָׁא֑וּל וַֽיִּשְׁמְר֥וּ אֶת־הַ֝בַּ֗יִת לַהֲמִיתֽוֹ׃
records.gloss: For the director, Do not destroy, of David, a miktam, when sent Saul and they watched the house to kill him.
pieces: For the music director. To the tune "Do Not Destroy." Of David. A miktam, from the time when Saul sent men to watch David's house in order to kill him.

L.1: For the director: "Do not destroy." Of David. A miktam, when Saul sent [men] and they watched the house to kill him.

R.1: For the leader of the music. To the tune "Do Not Destroy." A song of David, from the time when Saul sent men to watch his house so they could kill him.

decisions.reason: The title is part of the Hebrew text and is counted as verse 1, so the verse numbers here are one higher than in Bibles that print the title without a number.
As in 4:1.

decisions.choice: Do not destroy: probably the name of a tune
alternatives: a plea set at the head of the psalm
decisions.reason: The words ('al tashchet) also head Psalms 57, 59 and 75. They may name a melody the psalm was sung to. Moses prays the same words in Deuteronomy 9:26.

decisions.choice: miktam: a kind of psalm whose meaning is unknown
decisions.reason: As in 16:1. The word heads Psalms 16 and 56-60; its meaning is lost.

1 Samuel 19:11-17 tells how Saul sent men to watch David's house and kill him in the morning, and how Michal let him down through a window. Compare the enemies who prowl the city at evening (verses 7, 15) and the morning song (verse 17).
Balanced and Readable say that the words are probably the name of a tune (see the meaning decision).
Its meaning is unknown, so Readable says only that it is a song.
Balanced and Readable say who was sent and whose house it was.

records.heading: Rescue from enemies who prowl at night

records.gloss: Deliver me from my enemies, my God; from those rising against me you will set me on high.
pieces: Rescue me from my enemies, my God; \q lift me high out of reach of those who rise against me.

L.2: Deliver me from my enemies, my God; \q from those who rise up against me set me on high.

R.2: My God, save me from my enemies! \q Put me up high where the people attacking me cannot reach me.

decisions.choice: set me on high: put me out of reach
decisions.reason: The verb (sagav) means to be high, out of reach; the noun from it is "stronghold" in verses 10, 17 and 18.
The verb form can be a statement, "you will set me on high", but after "deliver me" it is a request.

records.source: הַ֭צִּילֵנִי מִפֹּ֣עֲלֵי אָ֑וֶן וּֽמֵאַנְשֵׁ֥י דָ֝מִ֗ים הוֹשִׁיעֵֽנִי׃
records.gloss: Deliver me from workers of wickedness, and from men of bloodshed save me.
pieces: Rescue me from those who do evil; \q save me from men who shed blood.

L.3: Deliver me from the workers of wickedness, \q and from men of blood save me.

R.3: Save me from people who do evil. \q Save me from killers.

decisions.reason: As in 5:7, 26:9 and 55:24, people ready to kill.

records.source: כִּ֤י הִנֵּ֪ה אָֽרְב֡וּ לְנַפְשִׁ֗י יָג֣וּרוּ עָלַ֣י עַזִ֑ים לֹא־פִשְׁעִ֖י וְלֹא־חַטָּאתִ֣י יְהוָֽה׃
records.gloss: For look, they lie in wait for my life; they stir up strife against me, strong [ones], not [for] my transgression and not [for] my sin, YHWH.
pieces: Look, they lie in ambush for my life; \q powerful men band together against me, \q though I have not rebelled or sinned, {{divine_name:LORD|Yahweh}}.

L.4: For look, they lie in wait for my soul; \q strong [men] stir up strife against me, \q not [for] my transgression and not [for] my sin, {{divine_name:LORD|Yahweh}}.

R.4: Look! They hide and wait to kill me. \q Strong men gang up on me, {{divine_name:LORD|Yahweh}}. \q But I have not done anything wrong to them.

decisions.choice: stir up strife: gather to attack
decisions.reason: The verb (gur) can mean to stir up strife or to gather as a band; either way they come together against him.

decisions.choice: not for my transgression: I am innocent
decisions.reason: The psalmist does not claim to be sinless, only that he has done nothing to deserve this attack (compare 7:4-6).
Balanced and Readable say "my life" for nefesh, as the convention allows.

records.source: בְּֽלִי־עָ֭וֺן יְרוּצ֣וּן וְיִכּוֹנָ֑נוּ ע֖וּרָה לִקְרָאתִ֣י וּרְאֵה׃
records.gloss: Without guilt they run and they set themselves; awake to meet me and see.
pieces: Through no fault of mine they rush to take up their places. \q Wake up, come to meet me, and look!

L.5: Without guilt [of mine] they run and set themselves; \q awake to meet me, and see.

R.5: I have done nothing wrong, but they run to get ready to attack. \q Wake up and come to help me! See what is happening!

decisions.reason: Calling on God to wake up (7:7; 44:24) is a bold way of asking him to act at once. It does not mean that God sleeps (121:4).

decisions.choice: to meet me: to come to my aid
decisions.reason: The verb (qara') means to meet, here to come to someone's side to help.

records.source: וְאַתָּ֤ה יְהוָֽה־אֱלֹהִ֥ים׀צְבָא֡וֹת אֱלֹ֘הֵ֤י יִשְׂרָאֵ֗ל הָקִ֗יצָה לִפְקֹ֥ד כָּֽל־הַגּוֹיִ֑ם אַל־תָּחֹ֨ן כָּל־בֹּ֖גְדֵי אָ֣וֶן סֶֽלָה׃
records.gloss: And you, YHWH God of hosts, God of Israel, awake to punish all the nations; do not be gracious to any treacherous [ones] of wickedness. Selah.
pieces: {{divine_name:LORD|Yahweh}} God of Armies, God of Israel, \q rise up and call all the nations to account; \q have no pity on any who plot evil in their treachery. Selah

L.6: And {{deity_pronoun:you|You}}, {{divine_name:LORD|Yahweh}} God of hosts, God of Israel, \q awake to punish all the nations; \q do not be gracious to any who treacherously work wickedness. Selah

R.6: {{divine_name:LORD|Yahweh}} God of Armies, God of Israel, \q wake up and punish all the nations! \q Do not show kindness to any of these evil traitors. Selah

decisions.reason: The title names the LORD as commander of the armies of heaven and of Israel. Literal keeps the older "hosts"; Balanced and Readable say "Armies", as in Psalm 46.

decisions.choice: all the nations: the enemies seen as part of a wider world
decisions.reason: The title speaks of Saul's men, but the prayer reaches out to all the nations, as in 9:6, 18. The psalm may have been sung later by Israel against foreign enemies; God judges all who do wrong.
The verb (bagad) is used of betraying trust (25:3).
Balanced and Readable begin with the address itself; the Hebrew "and you" puts weight on God, which the address keeps.

decisions.choice: Selah: a word whose meaning is no longer known
alternatives: lift up (the voice or the music)
decisions.reason: Selah stands at the end of a line 71 times in the Psalms and 3 times in Habakkuk 3. It is probably a direction for singing or music, perhaps a pause or an interlude; the ancient Greek translation renders it with a word meaning "interlude". It is not part of what is said, and here it marks a break after the line.
Its meaning is unknown (see the meaning decision on Selah), so every level keeps the word rather than guess, and keeps it apart from the sentence.

records.source: יָשׁ֣וּבוּ לָ֭עֶרֶב יֶהֱמ֥וּ כַכָּ֗לֶב וִיס֥וֹבְבוּ עִֽיר׃
records.gloss: They return at evening; they growl like the dog and go around [the] city.
pieces: At nightfall they return, \q snarling like dogs as they roam the city.

L.7: They return at evening; \q they growl like the dog and go around the city.

R.7: They come back every evening. \q They growl like dogs and prowl around the city.

decisions.reason: Dogs in ancient towns were mostly half-wild scavengers that roamed at night (22:17). To call enemies dogs is to call them dangerous and contemptible.
The verse is repeated in verse 15.

records.source: הִנֵּ֤ה׀יַבִּ֘יע֤וּן בְּפִיהֶ֗ם חֲ֭רָבוֹת בְּשִׂפְתוֹתֵיהֶ֑ם כִּי־מִ֥י שֹׁמֵֽעַ׃
records.gloss: Look, they pour out with their mouth; swords [are] on their lips, for, Who hears?
pieces: Look how their mouths gush with insults; \q their lips are swords, \q for they say, "Who will hear?"

L.8: Look, they pour [it] out with their mouth; \q swords [are] on their lips, \q for [they say], "Who hears?"

R.8: Listen to the cruel things they say! \q Their words cut like swords. \q They think, "No one can hear us."

decisions.reason: The verb (naba') is used of a spring bubbling up; their mouths pour out words without stopping (94:4).

alternatives: for who is listening? (the psalmist's comment)
decisions.reason: The question is best taken as what the enemies say: they think no one, not even God, is listening (10:11; 64:6).
The speakers are added to show whose words the question is (m2).

records.gloss: And you, YHWH, laugh at them; you mock at all [the] nations.
pieces: But {{deity_pronoun:you|You}}, {{divine_name:LORD|Yahweh}}, laugh at them; \q {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} hold all the nations in derision.

L.9: But {{deity_pronoun:you|You}}, {{divine_name:LORD|Yahweh}}, laugh at them; \q {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} mock at all [the] nations.

R.9: But {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} laugh at them, {{divine_name:LORD|Yahweh}}. \q You make fun of all the nations.

decisions.reason: God's laughter shows how small the plots of his enemies are next to his power (2:4; 37:13).

records.gloss: His strength — for you I will watch, for God [is] my stronghold.
pieces: Against his strength I will keep watch for {{deity_pronoun:you|You}}, \q for God is my high fortress.

L.10: [Because of] his strength I will watch for {{deity_pronoun:you|You}}, \q for God [is] my stronghold.

R.10: My enemy is strong, but I will watch for {{deity_pronoun:you|You}}, \q because God is my safe place high above.

alternatives: my Strength (some Hebrew manuscripts and ancient translations, as in verse 18)
decisions.reason: The Hebrew reads "his strength", most simply the enemy's strength, against which the psalmist waits for God. Verse 18, which repeats this verse, has "my Strength", meaning God, and some Hebrew manuscripts and ancient translations read that here too.
The word (misgav) is a high place out of an enemy's reach (9:10; 18:3).

decisions.choice: watch for you: wait and look out for you
decisions.reason: The verb (shamar) is used of a watchman; the psalmist waits for God as a guard waits for morning. Verse 18 has a word that sounds alike, "I will sing praises".
Readable says whose strength is meant (m1).

records.source: אֱלֹהֵ֣י חַסְדִּ֣י יְקַדְּמֵ֑נִי אֱ֝לֹהִ֗ים יַרְאֵ֥נִי בְשֹׁרְרָֽי׃
records.gloss: The God of my loyal love will meet me; God will let me look on my enemies.
pieces: My God of loyal love will go before me; \q God will let me look down on my foes.

L.11: The God of my loyal love will come to meet me; \q God will let me look on my enemies.

R.11: My God, who loves me faithfully, will come to my side. \q God will show me my enemies defeated.

decisions.choice: my loyal love: the word as read
decisions.reason: The words follow the form the Hebrew text's notes say to read, "my loyal love", as in verse 18; the written form differs slightly.
The word (chesed) is the love that keeps faith, God's commitment that does not give up (5:8). "The God of my loyal love" is the God whose loyal love is mine.

decisions.choice: let me look on my enemies: see them defeated
decisions.reason: To look on enemies is to see them overthrown (54:9; 92:12).

decisions.choice: meet me: come out to meet me, go before me
decisions.reason: The verb (qadam) means to come in front of someone, here to come to meet him with help (21:4).
As in the earlier psalms, Readable says "faithful love" for chesed.
Readable says what seeing the enemies means (m3).

records.source: אַל־תַּהַרְגֵ֤ם׀פֶּֽן־יִשְׁכְּח֬וּ עַמִּ֗י הֲנִיעֵ֣מוֹ בְ֭חֵילְךָ וְהוֹרִידֵ֑מוֹ מָֽגִנֵּ֣נוּ אֲדֹנָֽי׃
records.gloss: Do not kill them, lest they forget, my people; make them wander by your power and bring them down, our shield, my Lord.
pieces: Do not kill them outright, in case my people forget; \q by {{deity_pronoun:your|Your}} power send them staggering and bring them low, \q Lord, our shield.

L.12: Do not kill them, lest my people forget; \q make them wander by {{deity_pronoun:your|Your}} power and bring them down, \q our shield, my Lord.

R.12: Lord, {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} protect us like a shield. \q But do not kill them all at once, or my people will forget. \q Use {{deity_pronoun:your|Your}} power to make them wander and fall.

decisions.choice: do not kill them: let them be a lesson
decisions.reason: The psalmist asks that the enemies not be wiped out at once, so that their slow downfall may remind God's people of his justice. Verse 14 then asks for their end.

decisions.choice: make them wander: make them stagger as homeless
decisions.reason: The verb (nua') means to totter or wander, like Cain the wanderer (Genesis 4:12).
The shield is a common picture of God's protection (3:4; 18:3).
The Hebrew ('Adonai) is literally "my Lord", the usual way of addressing God; Literal keeps "my", Balanced and Readable say "Lord".

records.source: חַטַּאת־פִּ֗ימוֹ דְּֽבַר־שְׂפָ֫תֵ֥ימוֹ וְיִלָּכְד֥וּ בִגְאוֹנָ֑ם וּמֵאָלָ֖ה וּמִכַּ֣חַשׁ יְסַפֵּֽרוּ׃
records.gloss: [The] sin of their mouth, [the] word of their lips — and let them be caught in their pride, and for cursing and for lying they recount.
pieces: Every word from their lips is sin in their mouths; \q let them be snared by their own pride, \q for the cursing and lying they speak.

L.13: [For the] sin of their mouth, the word of their lips, \q let them be caught in their pride, \q and for [the] cursing and for [the] lying [that] they recount.

R.13: Everything they say is sinful. \q Let their pride become a trap for them, \q because of the curses and the lies that they speak.

decisions.choice: the sin of their mouth: every word is sin
alternatives: for the sin of their mouth, for the word of their lips
decisions.reason: The opening words stand without a verb. Most likely they mean that every word they speak is sin; they may also give the reason they should be caught.

decisions.choice: caught in their pride: trapped by their own arrogance
decisions.reason: As in 10:2, the wicked are to be caught in their own schemes.

records.source: כַּלֵּ֥ה בְחֵמָה֮ כַּלֵּ֪ה וְֽאֵ֫ינֵ֥מוֹ וְֽיֵדְע֗וּ כִּֽי־אֱ֭לֹהִים מֹשֵׁ֣ל בְּיַעֲקֹ֑ב לְאַפְסֵ֖י הָאָ֣רֶץ סֶֽלָה׃
records.gloss: Make an end in wrath, make an end, and they [will be] no more; and let them know that God [is] ruling in Jacob to [the] ends of the earth. Selah.
pieces: Destroy them in {{deity_pronoun:your|Your}} anger, destroy them until they are gone, \q so that people will know that God rules over Jacob \q to the ends of the earth. Selah

L.14: Make an end [of them] in wrath, make an end, and they [will be] no more; \q and let them know that God rules in Jacob \q to the ends of the earth. Selah

R.14: In {{deity_pronoun:your|Your}} anger, put an end to them. \q Finish them off, so that they are gone. \q Then everyone to the ends of the earth will know that God rules over Israel. Selah

decisions.choice: let them know: people will know
decisions.reason: "They" may be people everywhere, or the enemies themselves before their end. Either way, God's justice will be seen to the ends of the earth.

decisions.choice: rules in Jacob to the ends of the earth
decisions.reason: God rules from Jacob, that is Israel, and his rule reaches to the ends of the earth.
Balanced adds "your", since it is God's anger that is meant.
Readable uses the more familiar name of the people descended from Jacob.
Verse 12 asked God not to kill the enemies at once; here the psalmist asks for their end. The two belong together: first a lesson for God's people, then judgment.

decisions.choice: Selah: a word whose meaning is no longer known
alternatives: lift up (the voice or the music)
decisions.reason: Selah stands at the end of a line 71 times in the Psalms and 3 times in Habakkuk 3. It is probably a direction for singing or music, perhaps a pause or an interlude; the ancient Greek translation renders it with a word meaning "interlude". It is not part of what is said, and here it marks a break after the line.
Its meaning is unknown (see the meaning decision on Selah), so every level keeps the word rather than guess, and keeps it apart from the sentence.

records.source: וְיָשׁ֣וּבוּ לָ֭עֶרֶב יֶהֱמ֥וּ כַכָּ֗לֶב וִיס֥וֹבְבוּ עִֽיר׃
records.gloss: And they return at evening; they growl like the dog and go around [the] city.
pieces: At nightfall they return, \q snarling like dogs as they roam the city.

L.15: And they return at evening; \q they growl like the dog and go around the city.

R.15: They come back every evening. \q They growl like dogs and prowl around the city.

decisions.reason: The verse repeats verse 7. Verse 16 adds that they roam because they are hungry.

records.source: הֵ֭מָּה יְנִיע֣וּן לֶאֱכֹ֑ל אִם־לֹ֥א יִ֝שְׂבְּע֗וּ וַיָּלִֽינוּ׃
records.gloss: They wander about to eat; if not they are satisfied, then they spend the night.
pieces: They roam about for food, \q and if they are not filled, they stay out all night.

L.16: They wander about to eat; \q if they are not satisfied, they stay [all] night.

R.16: They wander around looking for food. \q If they do not find enough, they keep looking all night.

decisions.choice: they wander about: the word as read
decisions.reason: The word follows the form the Hebrew text's notes say to read; the written form differs slightly. The meaning is the same.

decisions.choice: spend the night: stay out all night
decisions.reason: The verb (lun) means to spend the night. The ancient Greek translation took it from a similar verb, "grumble" or "growl".

records.source: וַאֲנִ֤י׀אָשִׁ֣יר עֻזֶּךָ֮ וַאֲרַנֵּ֥ן לַבֹּ֗קֶר חַ֫סְדֶּ֥ךָ כִּֽי־הָיִ֣יתָ מִשְׂגָּ֣ב לִ֑י וּ֝מָנ֗וֹס בְּי֣וֹם צַר־לִֽי׃
records.gloss: And I will sing your strength and I will sing for joy in the morning [of] your loyal love, for you have been a stronghold for me and a refuge in [the] day of distress to me.
pieces: But I will sing of {{deity_pronoun:your|Your}} might, \q and at daybreak I will shout for joy over {{deity_pronoun:your|Your}} loyal love, \q for {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} have been my high fortress, \q a place to flee to when I was in trouble.

L.17: But I will sing of {{deity_pronoun:your|Your}} strength, \q and I will shout for joy in the morning [of] {{deity_pronoun:your|Your}} loyal love, \q for {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} have been a stronghold for me \q and a refuge in the day of my distress.

R.17: But I will sing about how strong {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} are. \q In the morning I will sing with joy about {{deity_pronoun:your|Your}} faithful love. \q You have kept me safe, \q a place I could run to when I was in trouble.

decisions.choice: in the morning: after the night of danger
decisions.reason: The enemies prowl at night (verses 7, 15-16); the psalmist sings in the morning, the time of God's help (46:6; 1 Samuel 19:11).
The word (chesed) is the love that keeps faith, God's commitment that does not give up (5:8).

decisions.choice: refuge: a place to flee to
decisions.reason: The word (manos) is a place of escape.
As in the earlier psalms, Readable says "faithful love" for chesed.

records.source: עֻ֭זִּי אֵלֶ֣יךָ אֲזַמֵּ֑רָה כִּֽי־אֱלֹהִ֥ים מִ֝שְׂגַּבִּ֗י אֱלֹהֵ֥י חַסְדִּֽי׃
records.gloss: My strength, to you I will sing praises, for God [is] my stronghold, [the] God of my loyal love.
pieces: My Strength, I will make music to {{deity_pronoun:you|You}}, \q for God is my high fortress, my God of loyal love.

L.18: My strength, to {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} I will sing praises, \q for God [is] my stronghold, the God of my loyal love.

R.18: God, {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} make me strong. I will sing praise to {{deity_pronoun:you|You}}. \q God keeps me safe. He is my God who loves me faithfully.

decisions.choice: my strength: a name for God
decisions.reason: The psalmist calls God "my Strength"; compare verse 10, where the Hebrew has "his strength".
The word (chesed) is the love that keeps faith, God's commitment that does not give up (5:8).
Verse 10 said "I will watch for you"; here the same refrain ends in praise: "I will sing praises to you".
As in the earlier psalms, Readable says "faithful love" for chesed.
Readable names God at the start, where the Hebrew addresses him as "my Strength".
